sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 18% to $19.5B, core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49), free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B), and management describes a 'really solid quarter' with a 'recovery plan in full swing.' However, full-year free cash flow guidance was not formally raised (management said 'we're not going to adjust that full year range right now'), and significant risks remain: China delivery uncertainty (~50 airplanes), tariff input costs (<$500M annually), and ongoing certification/quality issues. The positive trajectory is organic and structural, but the lack of a formal guidance raise and the explicit risks cap the score at moderately positive.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year, primarily reflecting higher commercial delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16); core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($1.13) in the prior year.
summary.guidance: Full-year free cash flow guidance not adjusted; management expects Q2 free cash flow roughly in line with Q1, with second half turning positive. 737 production expected to reach 38 per month over the next few months, with a request to increase to 42 per month later this year. 787 production expected to increase to 7 per month. 777X first delivery still anticipated in 2026. China delivery plan of ~50 airplanes for the balance of the year is being reassessed.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin 2.4% (vs. -0.5% prior year); core operating margin 1.0% (vs. -2.3% prior year). Commercial Airplanes operating margin -6.6% (vs. -24.6% prior year). Defense, Space & Security operating margin 2.5% (vs. 2.2% prior year). Global Services operating margin 18.6% (vs. 18.2% prior year).
key_risks: China delivery uncertainty: ~50 China deliveries in plan for the year, with customers indicating they will not take delivery due to tariffs.
Tariff input costs: net annual impact of higher tariffs on input costs is less than $500 million annually.
Seat certification issues affecting some 787 deliveries, expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
Ongoing certification programs for 737-7, 737-10, and 777X with no change to previously shared timelines.
Potential retaliatory tariffs from other countries beyond China could affect delivery ability.
SPS fire (Jenkintown fastener supplier) requiring alternate sourcing and re-qualification.
key_opportunities: F-47 win: selected by U.S. Air Force to design, build and deliver next-generation fighter aircraft, securing fighter franchise for decades.
Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture for $10.55 billion, strengthening balance sheet and focusing on core businesses.
Strong demand environment: backlog of $545 billion, with key commercial programs sold out into the next decade.
Production rate increases planned for 737 (to 38, then 42 per month) and 787 (to 7 per month).
Improved operational performance: 50% reduction in traveled work and 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
Defense portfolio well positioned with $62 billion backlog and stabilizing operational performance.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective' and 'I do like what I'm seeing,' while Brian West noted 'we had a really good start to the year' and 'we're still comfortable with the plan that we've outlined.'
